sections.summary: The past simple tense is used to describe completed actions in the past.

summary.en: Short answers respond to yes/no questions without repeating the whole sentence. They use the same auxiliary verb as the question.

en: Use the same auxiliary as the question (Do you? Yes, I do.)
Use be in short answers to be-questions (Is she? Yes, she is.)
Negative short answers use not (No, I don't.)
Use the correct subject pronoun (Are they? No, they aren't.)
Avoid answering with only Yes/No in formal speech (Yes, I am.)
Modal questions use the modal in the answer (Can you? Yes, I can.)

summary.en: Object pronouns receive the action of the verb. They appear after verbs or prepositions.

en: Object pronouns: me, you, him, her, it, us, them (I see him).
Use them after verbs (She calls me).
Use them after prepositions (The gift is for her).
Do not use object pronouns as subjects (He is right).
Place object pronouns before nouns they replace (I like it).
Use us/them for groups (He invited us).

en: Possessive pronouns: mine, yours, his, hers, its, ours, theirs (This is mine).
Do not use a noun after them (Not: mine book).
Do not use apostrophes (its is not it's).
Use them after be (The pen is hers).
They match the owner, not the object (Their car is theirs).
Use them to avoid repetition (Your bag is yours).

summary.en: After like, love, and hate, we often use the -ing form to talk about general preferences. This pattern is very common in everyday English.

en: Use verb-ing after like (I like swimming).
Use verb-ing after love (She loves reading).
Use verb-ing after hate (They hate waiting).
Use do/does for negatives (He doesn't like cooking).
Use do/does for questions (Do you like dancing?).
Add object after the gerund if needed (I like playing football).

برای سوال از do/does استفاده کنید (Do you like dancing?).
در صورت نیاز مفعول بعد از ing می‌آید (I like playing football).

summary.en: Can shows ability in the present. Could is used for past ability or polite requests. Both are easy ways to speak politely and clearly.

en: Use can for present ability (I can swim).
Use could for past ability (She could read at five).
Use can for simple requests (Can you help me?).
Use could for polite requests (Could you open the door?).
Modal verbs use base verb (He can speak English).
Negatives use cannot/can't (I can't come today).
Questions use can/could first (Can they wait?).

برای درخواست ساده از can استفاده کنید (Can you help me?).
برای درخواست مودبانه از could استفاده کنید (Could you open the door?).
بعد از مدال فعل پایه می‌آید (He can speak English).
منفی با cannot/can't است (I can't come today).
در سوال، can/could اول می‌آید (Can they wait?).

summary.en: Going to is used for future plans and intentions. It is also used for predictions with clear evidence. It is common in everyday speech.

en: Form: am/is/are + going to + base verb (I am going to study).

summary.en: Present simple talks about habits and facts. Present continuous talks about actions happening now or temporary situations. Choosing the right tense makes your meaning clear.
summary.fa: حال ساده برای عادت‌ها و حقیقت‌هاست. حال استمراری برای کارهای در حال انجام یا وضعیت موقت است. انتخاب درست زمان، معنی را واضح می‌کند.

en: Use present simple for routines (I go to work every day).
Use present simple for facts (Water boils at 100°C).
Use present continuous for actions now (She is studying now).
Use present continuous for temporary situations (He is living in Tehran this month).
Simple uses base verb or -s (He plays soccer).
Continuous uses am/is/are + ing (They are playing now).
Use time words to choose tense (usually = simple).

در حال ساده فعل پایه یا -s می‌آید (He plays soccer).
در حال استمراری از am/is/are + ing استفاده می‌شود (They are playing now).
از کلمات زمان کمک بگیرید (usually = حال ساده).

en: Form: was/were + verb-ing (I was studying).
Use was with I/he/she/it (She was cooking).
Use were with you/we/they (They were playing).
Use for an action at a past time (At 8, I was sleeping).
Use for background action (I was reading when he arrived).
Negatives: wasn't/weren't + ing (We weren't working).

برای عمل زمینه استفاده کنید (I was reading when he arrived).

summary.en: Past simple describes finished actions. Past continuous describes an action in progress. We often use them together to show a shorter action interrupting a longer one.
summary.fa: گذشته ساده عمل تمام‌شده را نشان می‌دهد. گذشته استمراری عمل در جریان را نشان می‌دهد. معمولاً برای قطع شدن یک عمل بلند با یک عمل کوتاه از هر دو استفاده می‌کنیم.

en: Use past simple for completed actions (I finished my homework).
Use past continuous for ongoing actions (I was studying).
Combine them with when (I was reading when he called).
Past continuous gives background (She was cooking).
Past simple shows the interrupting action (The phone rang).
Use time words like while/when (While I was walking, it started to rain).
fa: گذشته ساده برای عمل تمام‌شده است (I finished my homework).
گذشته استمراری برای عمل در جریان است (I was studying).
با when هر دو را ترکیب کنید (I was reading when he called).
گذشته استمراری عمل زمینه است (She was cooking).
گذشته ساده عمل کوتاه و قطع‌کننده است (The phone rang).
از while/when برای زمان استفاده کنید (While I was walking, it started to rain).

sections.summary: Articles are words that define nouns as specific or unspecific. English has two types: definite (the) and indefinite (a/an).
rules: Use "the" for specific nouns or when something is mentioned again
No article for plural/uncountable nouns in general statements
examples: I saw a dog. The dog was brown. (first mention → specific)
The sun rises in the east. (unique things)
I like coffee. (general - no article with uncountable)

commonMistakes.explanation: Student starts with consonant sound /st/, use "a"
No article when referring to the general purpose (education)

quiz.question: She is ___ honest person.
quiz.explanation: Honest starts with vowel sound /ɒ/, use "an"

quiz.question: I love ___ music.
quiz.explanation: General statements with uncountable nouns need no article

sections.summary: Prepositions show relationships between nouns and other words. The most common are in, on, at.
rules: Place: at (specific points), on (surfaces), in (enclosed spaces)
at: at 3 PM, at night, at home, at the door
on: on Monday, on the table, on the wall
in: in May, in 2020, in the morning, in the room
examples: I wake up at 7 AM. (specific time)
The book is on the table. (surface)
He lives in New York. (city/enclosed space)

commonMistakes.wrong: I will see you in Monday.
commonMistakes.correct: I will see you on Monday.
commonMistakes.explanation: Use "on" with days of the week

commonMistakes.wrong: The class starts at the morning.
commonMistakes.correct: The class starts in the morning.
commonMistakes.explanation: Use "in" with parts of the day (except "at night")

quiz.question: The party is ___ Saturday night.
quiz.explanation: Use "on" with specific days and nights of the week
